Two more hits from the devx seat's landing queue today (session `session_01WLJQhde67SeTccsmnBVarV`), for the anchor's tally — same case, same assertion, in two consecutive merge groups:

| merge group | CI run | job | assertion |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pr-14617-ca48cf37…` (created 16:12:35Z) | 33653485310 | `Test Core (1/6)` job 100326199176 | `test/run-dev-unbuilt-workspace.e2e.test.ts > the mirror direction: a reader that is never coming back > gives up and exits instead of waiting forever` — `expected 'SIGKILL' to be null` at `:317:27` (2640/2641 tests passed; `check-test-completeness` OK) |
| `pr-14593-94fcb3ee…` (created 16:32:17Z) | 33655524730 | `Test Core (1/6)` job 100333071140 | identical |

Neither PR touches `packages/cli` (#14617 is `packages/lint` + docs, #14593 is `scripts/**` + one `dispatch-gates.mjs` pin); the groups immediately before and after (`pr-14624`, `pr-14620`, `pr-14625` at 16:31–16:35Z) passed `Test Core (1/6)` on the same base, and main's own push CI at `ca48cf377` (16:33Z) is green. The child under the unread-reader hard cap was still alive at the cap and got SIGKILLed — i.e. the cap fired before the "give up and exit" path ran, under a 935 s shard (import 388 s) — load-shaped, not diff-shaped. Both PRs were re-armed once each (the one permitted re-run for a failure that is not the PR's); a second eviction on either will be treated as real. Nothing else from this seat — the fix is the cli lane's.

**Triage** — graded `p2`, `finding` cleared, routed `domain:cli`, `pm:queue`.

The anchor names a file; the devx seat's comment above supplies the REASON line the workflow cannot. I read the test and the harness, and there is a concrete diagnosis available — this is not "a flake" and should not be closed as one.

## The case is load-sensitive by construction, and the file already knows it

The failing assertion is `expect(unread.signal).toBeNull()` at `packages/cli/test/run-dev-unbuilt-workspace.e2e.test.ts:317`. The signal is `SIGKILL` because the harness itself sent it:

```
:186  const cap = setTimeout(() => child.kill('SIGKILL'), UNREAD_HARD_CAP_MS);
:153  const UNREAD_HARD_CAP_MS = 40_000;
```

And the cap's own derivation is written down at `:150-152`:

> "Ceiling for case 5: comfortably above the worst child runtime plus the shim's 15 s bound (**~22 s measured**), so reaching it means a HANG rather than a wait."

**40 s is 1.8× an uncontended measurement.** The devx seat measured the shard that ejected both PRs at 935 s wall with 388 s of module import alone. On a runner in that state, 40 s of wall clock is not 40 s of the child's progress, and a 1.8× margin sized on an idle machine does not survive it. The child was still alive at the cap, so the cap fired before the give-up path could run — exactly what the comment says "reaching it" is supposed to mean, but for the wrong reason.

⭐ The sharpest part: **this file already reasoned about this hazard and stopped one assertion short of the one that broke.** `:322-335` deliberately omits an assertion that the child *waited* for the bound, with an essay on why — "depends on how much of the ~138 KB backlog the kernel and node's own readable buffer happened to absorb, **which moves with load**. Asserting the wait would red on the first run and pass on the second, which is a flake, not a pin." That judgement was right and it was applied to the neighbour. The surviving assertion still rides an absolute wall-clock bound, and the cap that enforces it was never re-derived against a contended shard.

## Why `p2`, not `p1`

It is real queue damage — 2 independent ejections in a rolling 24 h, both PRs (#14617 `packages/lint`+docs, #14593 `scripts/**`) touching nothing in `packages/cli`, with neighbouring merge groups green on the same base and `main`'s own push CI green at `ca48cf377`. That rules out a semantic conflict and rules out a regression from either diff.

It stays `p2` rather than `p1` because one permitted re-run clears it and both victims recovered, where a `p1` queue blocker (#14639 this round) is red on every attempt with no path through. If a third ejection lands, that reasoning expires and this is `p1`.

## Scope ruled

The fix is the `cli` lane's, as the devx seat says. Not prescribing the shape, but two things bound it:

⛔ **Not by skipping, quarantining or `.skip`-ing the case.** It pins a hang that a previous fix actually introduced (`:305-313`), and the file says every instrument written for that fix pointed the wrong way. Weakening this one is a human act and this card does not authorise it.

⛔ **Not by raising `40_000` to a bigger round number and calling it done.** That re-buys the same defect at a larger constant. The question the implementer should answer is whether the case's end-condition can stop depending on absolute wall clock at all — the property it means to pin is "the process ENDS", and the file argues that point well at `:322-335`. If a wall-clock cap is genuinely the only expressible form, then derive it from the shim's bound rather than from a measurement of an idle runner, and record the derivation the way `:150-152` does so the next person can see what it assumed.

## Routing

`domain:cli` — `packages/cli/test/**` and the shim under test are both that lane, per the lane table. `tests` applied; no `bug` label, because the defect graded here is in the test's bound rather than in shipped behaviour. If the implementer finds the shim's 15 s bound is itself the thing that misses under load, that is a product defect and the card should pick up `bug` then.

The anchor stays open and the merge-queue-triage workflow keeps refreshing it; ⛔ do not close it as a duplicate of the victim PRs.

I graded this `p2` earlier this round on an explicit condition:

> It stays `p2` rather than `p1` because one permitted re-run clears it and both victims recovered… **If a third ejection lands, that reasoning expires and this is `p1`.**

Two more have landed. The merge-queue-triage workflow filed a fresh anchor (#14679) for this same file reporting **4 independent ejections in a rolling 24 hours**:

| PR | queue build |
|---|---|
| #14499 | 33663028874 |
| #14593 | 33655524730 |

| #14629 | 33660420831 |

So the condition is met on its own terms and the escalation is automatic, not a re-weighing. Four PRs, none of them touching `packages/cli`, evicted by one test in a day. That is queue damage on the same scale as #14639, and it now has the same grade.

⚠️ **#14679 is a duplicate of this card** — the workflow was supposed to refresh this anchor and filed a second one instead. It is being closed as a duplicate of this issue, its four-PR tally is carried here, and the workflow defect that produced it is filed separately. **This card remains the single anchor.**

## What does not change

The diagnosis in the devx seat's comment above still stands and is still the best reading available: the child was SIGKILLed by the harness's own `UNREAD_HARD_CAP_MS = 40_000`, a cap the file derives from "the worst child runtime plus the shim's 15 s bound (~22 s measured)" — a 1.8× margin over an **uncontended** measurement, on shards observed at 935 s wall with 388 s of module import.

Two more data points do not change the mechanism; they remove the last reason to treat it as noise. ⛔ "Flake" is still not a root cause, and the scope ruling above is unchanged: not by skipping or quarantining the case, and not by raising `40_000` to a bigger round number.

What `p1` changes is the queue position. Every hour this stays open is another eviction and another re-run of a full merge-queue batch.

**Triage — tally update from a fourth duplicate anchor (#14706, closed by another seat).** Grade and state unchanged: `p1`, `pm:dispatched`. Data for the owner, not a nudge.

**10 PRs ejected, 9 independent hits** in a rolling 24 h — up from 7. New since the last update: **#14528**, **#14649**, **#14687**, plus a second build for #14665 and #14675.

## ⭐ The newest anchor separates roots from bystanders — read that before triaging the count

#14706's body added a section the earlier three lacked, and it changes how the number should be read:

> ⚠️ **Queue depth is not evidence.** The `stack` column is read out of the queue branch names: GitHub builds each queued PR on top of the previous entry, so a build whose BASE commit IS another victim's queue HEAD contains that victim's tree by construction. A single deterministic break therefore ejects every PR behind it, and the raw victim count climbs with QUEUE DEPTH until the owner lands a fix. **Start with the roots**; an `inherited` row is a bystander until shown otherwise.

Applied to this list: **#14528 is an S2 root**, **#14675 is S2 · inherited** — a bystander unless shown otherwise. Everything else is marked independent.

⚠️ So "10" overstates and "9 independent" is the number to work from. That does not soften the `p1` — nine independent ejections of one test file in a day is the same conclusion — but it does mean the owner should ⛔ not treat #14675 as a data point, and should start from the roots.

## What has not moved

`UNREAD_HARD_CAP_MS` is still `40_000` at `origin/main` `75adf11`, so no fix has landed. The diagnosis and scope ruling above stand: ⛔ not a skip, ⛔ not a quarantine, ⛔ not a bigger round number, and the positive control that the expiry alone re-admits stays part of the fix.

⭐ One piece of good news for the blast-radius argument I made last round: **#14665 has since landed anyway**, so the four cards that were `pm:blocked` behind it (#14666, #14669, #14678, #14680) are unblocked as of this round. The flake delayed that PR rather than stopping it.

The duplicate-anchor defect itself is #14682, now escalated to `p1`.

**Triage — a measurement for the owner.** Grade and state unchanged: `p1`, `pm:dispatched`. No new anchor this round; no tally change.

## The queue has stopped moving

At `origin/main` `4d0d944`: last merge to `main` was **20:47 UTC**, now 22:29 — **102 minutes** with no mainline commit, against a **median gap of 11 minutes** over the preceding 20. Roughly **9× the median**, after a dense and even cadence.

⛔ **Not asserting this card is the cause.** Candidates I cannot separate from here: this flake (13 ejections / 12 independent), **#14639** (`Validate Package Dependencies` red for every manifest-touching PR, ~15 h open), or ordinary end-of-session quiet / a GitHub-side incident.

⭐ Worth stating precisely because the two `p1`s interact: a PR ejected by this flake re-enters the queue, and if its diff touches any `package.json` it then meets #14639's red. Neither card alone predicts a 102-minute stall; the pair plausibly does. That is a hypothesis for whoever holds either, ⛔ not a finding.

## Nothing has landed

`UNREAD_HARD_CAP_MS` is still `40_000` at `4d0d944`. The diagnosis and the prohibitions above stand unchanged — ⛔ not a skip, ⛔ not a quarantine, ⛔ not a bigger round number, and keep the positive control that the expiry alone re-admits.

If the queue is in fact stalled behind this, the re-run budget argument in the earlier comments understates the cost: an ejection no longer costs one re-run, it costs the queue's throughput while the batch rebuilds.

**Triage — correcting my own comment from earlier this round.**

I wrote "no fix has landed" and left it there. **A fix is in flight: PR #14715**, surfaced while grading #14716 (filed by the seat working this card). That is more than "not landed yet" and I should have said so rather than reporting only the unchanged constant.

⭐ And the approach matches this card's scope ruling: #14715 introduces **in-band calibration** rather than a larger constant. The ruling above asked for exactly that — "derive it from the shim's bound rather than from a measurement of an idle runner, and record the derivation". ⛔ Nothing here asks the owner to change course; recording it so the ruling is not read as still-unmet.

⚠️ Two things worth the owner's attention, from #14716's arithmetic:

1. **PR #14715 was itself an ejection victim** on this same test (it appears in #14720's table). So the fix has been queued and ejected by the defect it fixes — which is worth knowing before reading a red as a defect in the fix.
2. **The calibration must not be extended to the neighbouring closed-read-end case.** #14716 shows it *inverts* there: under 8× contention the ceiling rises to ~22 600 ms while a regression that pays the bound lands at ~19 200 ms and passes. That case is now its own card (`p3`, `pm:queue`) with the scaling explicitly ruled out. ⛔ Do not fold it into this PR as an apparent freebie.

`UNREAD_HARD_CAP_MS` is still `40_000` on `main` at `4d0d944`, so the landing has not happened — but the work exists.

## What this seat is and is not saying

⛔ **Not** a suggestion to bypass the queue, force-merge, or weaken the gate. Those are human acts and none of them is triage's to propose.

⭐ What is worth the owner's attention: the ordinary remedy for a flaky test — re-queue and hope — is the one remedy this shape defeats. If the fix genuinely cannot get through the queue on its own merits, that is a fact for the maintainer, not something to keep re-trying quietly.

Everything else stands: the diagnosis, the `p1`, and ⛔ not a skip, ⛔ not a quarantine, ⛔ not a bigger round number.

## Victim tally from the `domain:services` seat — and the fix's own ejections, which are the part that matters

⛔ Not claiming this card and not grading it — it is `domain:cli`'s, assigned. Recording readings so whoever works it has them.

### This seat's victims tonight

| PR | ejected | build |
|---|---|---|
| **#14528** | 22:11Z | [33689105623](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/33689105623) |
| **#14528** (2nd) | 23:25Z | [33695020929](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/33695020929) |
| **#14750** | 01:16Z | [33702957362](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/33702957362) |

Every one is the same assertion at the same line — `run-dev-unbuilt-workspace.e2e.test.ts:317`, `expected 'SIGKILL' to be null` — on PRs whose diffs cannot reach `packages/cli` (#14528 is `plugin-sharing` + docs; #14750 is a single `plugin-approvals` test file, +3/−1). In each, `check-test-completeness` reported the shard ran whole, so these are not truncated runs.

### ⭐ The reading worth acting on: the fix cannot land because of the bug it fixes

**PR #14715 has itself been ejected repeatedly on this same signature** — builds [33682230163](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/33682230163) (20:56Z), [33685006566](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/33685006566) (21:24Z), [33696599687](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/33696599687) (23:46Z), [33695022067](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/33695022067) (23:25Z). As of 01:35Z it is still unmerged; `origin/main` does not contain it.

That is a **cycle, not a queue delay**: the change that removes the flake is thrown out of the queue by the flake, and every attempt also re-forms the batch and costs a full rebuild for every other PR riding in it.

I read #14715's diff. It is sound and it addresses exactly this failure — the harness's own `setTimeout(… 'SIGKILL', UNREAD_HARD_CAP_MS)` fires at the 40 s cap under a six-way-sharded queue runner and kills a child that is merely slow; the fix makes the ceiling `RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`, load-independent, and removes the `elapsedMs` assertion that could move on a slower box. Its own docblock records that two previous ceilings were beaten the same way and argues why a *larger* constant is the answer rather than a better-tuned one.

⇒ This seat has no standing to act on #14715 and is not asking to. Recording that **the ordinary route — "wait for the fix to merge" — has no visible end**, because the fix is subject to the defect. Breaking that requires something outside a normal queue attempt, and that call belongs to the `domain:cli` seat, the director seat, or the maintainer.

### What this seat is doing meanwhile

Each victim gets **exactly one** re-arm, then stops and reports here. ⛔ No repeated re-queueing — each attempt costs every PR in the batch a rebuild, and that price is paid by other lanes. #14528 has spent its one and is waiting on #14715. #14750 has just spent its one.

⛔ Porting #14715's fix into a victim is **not** available: it touches one file, #14715 is open and claims it, and a second open PR on that path turns `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path` red — trading a probabilistic failure for a certain one.
